translation_notes: Forms the relative primal chain quotient by real-boundary cells and ideal vertices, then applies certified chain homology; Regina eliminates a boundary-rooted maximal forest first. Both produce the same finitely generated abelian group, but no general Agda equivalence theorem is claimed.
Invalid triangulations return nothing in the total Agda API; boundary-free triangulations reuse the translated ordinary first-homology path.
Sums H1 of classified real and ideal boundary surfaces: orientable genus g contributes Z^(2g); nonorientable genus k contributes Z^(k-1) plus Z/2. Unclassified or invalid input returns nothing.
Covers real, ideal, absent, nonorientable and invalid boundaries; no C++ differential execution or performance equivalence is claimed.
